sources.title: Mathematics of Public Key Cryptography, Version 2.0
sources.citation: Steven D. Galbraith, Mathematics of Public Key Cryptography, extended and corrected version 2.0, 31 October 2018.
sources.notes: User-supplied 696-page PDF read in full-text form. The reproducible inventory indexes 717 numbered results and 375 section headings; promoted claims below are paraphrases with exact result or section locators.

nodes.label: Representation and product DLP
nodes.statement: The representation problem asks for bounded coefficients expressing a target as a product of supplied generators; the product DLP asks for bounded factors whose product is the hidden exponent.
nodes.scope: Finitely generated abelian groups with explicitly supplied coefficient sets; neither problem is identical to an unrestricted single-generator DLP instance.

nodes.label: Generic representation lower bound
nodes.statement: For even l and equal coefficient-set sizes s, a generic algorithm solving the representation problem with success at least 1/log(s)^c needs Omega(s^(l/2)/log(s)^(c/2)) group operations.
nodes.scope: Generic group model, even l, equally sized coefficient sets, and the stated noticeable-success convention; the proof embeds an ordinary DLP through base-s digits.

nodes.label: Low-Hamming-weight DLP
nodes.statement: Given g and h, recover an exponent of bit length at most n and Hamming weight at most w such that h equals g raised to that exponent.
nodes.scope: An augmented distributional promise on the exponent; it does not describe uniformly sampled full-width ECDLP scalars.

nodes.label: Coppersmith low-weight meet-in-the-middle
nodes.statement: Random balanced splittings give expected O(sqrt(w) times binomial(n/2,w/2)) exponentiations and O(binomial(n/2,w/2)) stored group elements for the low-Hamming-weight DLP.
nodes.scope: Even n and w after harmless padding, with the promised low-weight exponent; the bound includes the probability that a random split balances the support.

nodes.label: Wagner four-sum cube-root heuristic
nodes.statement: For four sufficiently random n-bit lists satisfying the pair-product size condition, Wagner's representation-aware filtering is expected to solve four-sum in soft-O(2^(n/3)) time and space.
nodes.scope: XOR bit-string representation with random-list and list-size hypotheses. The speedup exploits visible low bits and is explicitly not a generic-group DLP algorithm.
assumptions: Each adjacent list-size product is at least 2^(2 ceil(n/3))

nodes.label: Rigorous three-partition rho bound
nodes.statement: For every fixed failure tolerance epsilon, the original three-set rho walk finds a collision in O_epsilon(sqrt(r) log(r)^3) group operations with probability at least 1-epsilon over the random partition.
nodes.scope: Theorem 14.2.23's random choice of a three-set partition. It does not prove the precise random-mapping constant for a fixed cheap partition used in an implementation.

nodes.label: Gaudry-Schost two-dimensional walk
nodes.statement: For a logarithm represented by two unknown coefficients in an N by N box, the tame/wild Gaudry-Schost collision method has quoted average cost about (2.43+o(1))N group operations.
nodes.scope: Average case under Heuristic 14.7.4's independent uniform sampling of the tame and wild regions; this is a structured-range problem, not full-width ECDLP.

nodes.label: Subexponential L notation
nodes.statement: L_N(alpha,c) denotes exp((c+o(1))(log N)^alpha(log log N)^(1-alpha)), separating polynomial, subexponential, and exponential regimes by alpha.
nodes.scope: Asymptotic notation; the hidden o(1), parameter path, and cost unit must be fixed before using it as a concrete security estimate.

nodes.label: Fixed-base Diffie-Hellman
nodes.statement: Fixed-CDH keeps the generator fixed as part of the problem family, while ordinary CDH permits the generator to vary with the instance.
nodes.scope: Prime-order algebraic groups or algebraic-group quotients under the book's granularity convention.

nodes.label: CDH random self-reducibility
nodes.statement: A CDH instance in a cyclic group can be randomized uniformly by exponent and offset blinding, and a solution to the randomized instance can be unblinded to solve the original.
nodes.scope: Cyclic group with known order and nonidentity generator; this is a problem reduction, not a lower bound on CDH.

nodes.label: CDH success amplification
nodes.statement: A CDH or Fixed-CDH oracle with inverse-polylogarithmic success can be amplified to high success using random self-reductions and consistency checks, with the explicit query and residual-error bounds of Theorem 21.3.8.
nodes.scope: Prime-order group, fixed inverse-polylogarithmic starting success, and the theorem's target error epsilon-prime greater than 1/r.

nodes.label: den Boer DLP-to-Fixed-CDH reduction
nodes.statement: A perfect Fixed-CDH oracle yields a DLP algorithm whose extra group cost is governed by the largest prime factor l of r-1, with a square-root-in-l tradeoff.
nodes.scope: Prime-order subgroup and a perfect Fixed-CDH oracle. The reduction is polynomial only for suitable smoothness of r-1; it does not prove CDH and DLP equivalent for every group family.
assumptions: Cost depends on the largest prime factor of r-1
nodes.formula: group cost = O(sqrt(l) log(r)^2/log(l)); oracle queries = O(log(r)log log(r))

nodes.label: Maurer auxiliary-curve reduction
nodes.statement: A perfect Fixed-CDH oracle solves DLP in expected polylogarithmic oracle queries when an auxiliary elliptic curve over F_r has known cyclic B-smooth order; a family-level equivalence follows when such auxiliary orders are polylog-smooth.
nodes.scope: Requires constructing the auxiliary curve, knowing its order, cyclicity, and the stated smoothness. The broad equivalence is conditional on those family-level auxiliary inputs, not on ECDLP hardness alone.

nodes.label: Static-DH auxiliary-power attack
nodes.statement: Repeated static-DH queries generate correlated powers of the hidden exponent; if d divides r-1, d queries combine with a meet-in-the-middle step costing about (sqrt((r-1)/d)+sqrt(d))log(r) group operations.
nodes.scope: Static-DH oracle for one fixed secret and a divisor d of r-1. This is an augmented-oracle attack, not an upper bound for plain CDH or ECDLP.

nodes.label: Least-significant DLP bit is as hard as DLP
nodes.statement: A perfect oracle returning the least significant bit of a prime-order discrete logarithm can be queried iteratively to recover the entire logarithm.
nodes.scope: Prime-order group and a perfect bit oracle under the book's integer representative convention; predictive or noisy-bit variants require separate hard-core-bit analysis.

nodes.label: Efficient isogeny transports ECDLP
nodes.statement: An efficiently computable isogeny of degree not divisible by subgroup order r maps an order-r DLP instance injectively to the codomain, so a codomain DLP oracle solves the source instance.
nodes.scope: Same-order curves over the same finite field, computable isogeny, and degree coprime to r. Large conductor gaps can prevent efficient isogeny computation, so equal curve order alone is insufficient.
assumptions: r does not divide the isogeny degree

nodes.label: Pairing bilinearity and nondegeneracy
nodes.statement: The Weil and reduced Tate-Lichtenbaum pairings are bilinear and nondegenerate on their stated torsion subgroups and quotient domains, subject to their field and coprimality hypotheses.
nodes.scope: The exact domains differ between the Weil and Tate-Lichtenbaum pairings; alternation of the Weil pairing can prevent using the same source point twice.
assumptions: Torsion order coprime to field characteristic

nodes.label: Pairing decision reduction
nodes.statement: A nondegenerate pairing efficiently solves co-DDH when the two source points generate independent r-torsion directions; DDH in one source subgroup is easy only when a suitable self-pairing or distortion map supplies a nontrivial second direction.
nodes.scope: Full rational r-torsion for the Weil-pairing argument or another suitable pairing domain. Pairings do not automatically solve DDH in every ordinary elliptic-curve subgroup.
assumptions: Suitable independent torsion point or distortion map

nodes.label: Pairing-friendly security is two-sided
nodes.statement: Pairing-friendly parameters must make both the source elliptic-curve DLP and the target finite-field DLP hard while keeping the pairing and representations efficient.
nodes.scope: Parameter-selection dependency, not a claim that either DLP is hard; target-field security must use the best finite-field algorithm and the actual embedding field.

edges.statement: The bound applies to the representation branch under its equal-set generic-model hypotheses.
Structured multi-generator and product-exponent instances need separate distributions and bounds from ordinary ECDLP.
The meet-in-the-middle cost exploits the promised exponent support.
A low-weight scalar distribution can be much weaker than uniform full-width scalar sampling.
Wagner is a concrete example of a representation-aware algorithm escaping a generic birthday lower bound.
It supplies a rigorous asymptotic collision bound for a random three-partition but not the heuristic constant of a fixed implementation.
The two-dimensional range geometry changes the walk constant while retaining square-root-in-domain-size behavior.
L notation supplies the asymptotic vocabulary used to distinguish subexponential index-calculus regimes.
The fixed-generator granularity must be explicit in reductions and preprocessing claims.
Random-instance CDH success transfers to arbitrary instances by blinding.
Random self-reductions generate the trials used by the amplification theorem.
The reduction upgrades noticeable-success CDH or Fixed-CDH oracles before using perfect-oracle reductions.
Under the r-1 factorization condition, DLP is reduced to Fixed-CDH plus the stated residual work.
The largest factor of r-1 determines whether this is a polynomial equivalence or only a tradeoff.
An auxiliary smooth-order curve turns a Fixed-CDH oracle into a DLP solver.
The auxiliary curve construction and smoothness hypothesis control the reduction's applicability.
Repeated use of one fixed secret exposes a stronger oracle than a single ordinary CDH challenge.
A perfect least-significant-bit oracle suffices to recover the full logarithm.
A computable isogeny of degree coprime to r transports the source subgroup DLP to the codomain.
Efficient transport along individual isogenies is the local step behind isogeny-class random reductions.
Bilinearity carries the logarithm into the target group and nondegeneracy prevents collapse.
The pairing compares exponents when a nontrivial second direction is available.
DDH becomes easy only for pairing domains with a nontrivial self-pairing or distortion map; co-DDH is the general two-source statement.
Efficient decision pairings are the standard mechanism for gap-DH groups.
Target-field DLP strength is a separate parameter-selection obligation after the pairing transfer.
Both source and target groups must be priced under their best known attacks.

research_targets.label: Representation-aware relation filter
research_targets.objective: Construct or rule out a coordinate-visible filter for elliptic-curve relation search that has Wagner's decisive property: qualifying pairs can be enumerated in subquadratic time at the required density, and the filter is not simulable from generic group operations and equality alone.
research_targets.acceptance: Freeze an infinite parameter family; prove filter density, enumeration time, relation yield and end-to-end memory exponents; give either a non-generic-interface witness or a generic simulation; compare against the matched pair-table and random-base controls.
research_targets.next_step: Translate the five-property generalized Wagner checklist on pp. 283-284 into tests for the current Semaev membership, PKM, small-abscissa and pair-table predicates; the existing generic-interface audit already rules out accepting a renamed group-law table as the witness.
